units.la: XIII. Potentia. §. A. 1. 2. Cogitationis creatæ vi, nil extra illam existens poni, quamquam cum ea quædam existant. 3. Non ita de Cogitatione summa. 142
units.tr: XIII. Power. §. A. 1. 2. By the force of created thought, nothing is posited as existing outside it, although certain things exist together with it. 3. It is not so with the supreme Thought.

units.la: §, D. 4.5.6. Res vi voluntatis Divinæ poni demonstratur. 7. Potentia Dei triplex consideratio. 8. Una, Potentia absoluta, de qua nil determinandum. 9. Altera in respectu ad rerum essentiam. de hac quatuor Propositiones. 10. Prima. 11. Secunda. 12. Tertia. 13. 14. Quarta, ubi obiter de Potentia Dei in Mysterio Transsubstantiationis. 15. Ultima Divinæ Potentiæ consideratio. Omnia existere quia Deus vult. 16. Qua existunt in maximis & minimis, in substantiis & modis, ab illo effici. 143
units.tr: §, D. 4.5.6. It is shown that things are posited by the will of God. 7. The power of God considered in three ways. 8. First, the absolute power, about which nothing is to be determined. 9. Second, in respect to the essence of things; concerning this, four propositions. 10. The first. 11. The second. 12. The third. 13–14. The fourth, where in passing we speak of the power of God in the mystery of Transubstantiation. 15. The last consideration of the divine power: that all things exist because God wills it. 16. That by which they exist, in the greatest and the least things, in substances and in modes, is effected by him.

units.la: §. 17. De Potentia Dei quæstiones. Prima, De modo ponendi res. 18. 19. Secunda. Res poni sub conditionibus, nec media physica vel moralia excludi. 20. De miraculis. 21. 22. 23. De iis Physicæ spectatis. Ea, (neque ob mysterium Transsubstantiationis) non evertere naturam, ejusve leges. 24. De iis ad cultum Dei relatis Propositiones Quatuor. 25. Quæstio Tertia, de rerum Necessitate & Contingentia. 26. Quarta, quid Creatio, Conservatio, Concursus prævius, simultaneus? 27. Difficultates. De libertate. 28. De compensatione, laude, existimatione creaturarum. 29. De petitione, gratiarum actione, &c. 30. Deus omnia; ab aliis nil sperandum vel metuendum. 158
units.tr: §. 17. Questions concerning the power of God. First, on the manner of positing things. 18. 19. Second: things are posited under conditions, and neither physical nor moral means are excluded. 20. On miracles. 21. 22. 23. On those considered physically: these (and not on account of the mystery of Transubstantiation) do not overturn nature or its laws. 24. On those related to the worship of God, four propositions. 25. The third question, on the necessity and contingency of things. 26. The fourth: what are Creation, Conservation, and prior and simultaneous concurrence? 27. Difficulties. On liberty. 28. On the compensation, praise, and esteem of creatures. 29. On petition, thanksgiving, etc. 30. God is all things; nothing is to be hoped for or feared from others.

units.la: XIV. Cognitio seu Scientia. §. A. 1. 2. 3. De cognitione Mentis creatæ. Cur non ad omnes res extenditur. 4. Cognitionis adæquatio & angustia. 5. Ignorantia. Obscuritas. Error. Ratiocinatio. Incertitudo. Opinio. Evidentia. Certitudo. Scientia. 6. Nil de eo quod in hac vita cognitioni nostræ accidet, determinandum. 172
units.tr: XIV. Knowledge or Science. §. A. 1. 2. 3. Of the knowledge of the created mind. Why it does not extend to all things. 4. The adequacy and narrowness of knowledge. 5. Ignorance. Obscurity. Error. Reasoning. Uncertainty. Opinion. Evidence. Certainty. Science. 6. Nothing is to be determined concerning what will befall our knowledge in this life. 172

units.la: §. D. 7. 8. 9. Cognitio Dei libera, independens, universalis, particularis, adæquata, certa, infallibilis, immutabilis. 10. Quibus rebus cognitio nostra potissimum sit applicanda? 178
units.tr: §. D. 7. 8. 9. The knowledge of God: free, independent, universal, particular, adequate, certain, infallible, immutable. 10. To which matters should our knowledge chiefly be applied? 178

units.la: §.D.3. Sapientia Dei. 4. Ejus perfectiones. 5. Quaedam meliora, sed non sapientius fieri potuissent. 6. Duo extrema vitanda. 7. Prius. 8. Posterius. Consilia & fines Dei non scrutanda. 9. Nulli Dei in quibuscunque fines inquirendi, praeter placitum ejus. 182
units.tr: §.D.3. The wisdom of God. 4. His perfections. 5. Some things could have been better, but could not have been made wiser. 6. Two extremes to be avoided. 7. The first. 8. The second. The counsels and ends of God are not to be searched out. 9. No one may inquire into God's ends, whatever they may be, apart from his good pleasure.

units.la: XVI. Æternitas. §. A. 1. Ex variabilitate mentis occasiones ad sequentia. 2. Temporis natura, mensura. Successio. prolongatio. effluxus. 3. Mens subtrahenda tempori ad adumbrationem Æternitatis. 187
units.tr: XVI. Eternity. §. A. 1. Occasions for the following arise from the variability of the mind. 2. The nature and measure of time. Succession, prolongation, outflow. 3. The mind must be withdrawn from time to form an image of Eternity. 187

units.la: §.D.4. Dei Æternitas demonstratur. 5. Ejus Idea. Boëthii definitio non exacta. 6. Æternitas non coexistit tempori, nec hoc illi. 7. Essentia rerum non sunt proprie æternæ. 8. Res in Æternitate factæ non sunt. 9. Si mundus non haberet initium existentia, non tamen esset æternus. Demonstratur habere initium. 10. Figmentorum circa Æternitatem & praesentiam Dei, origines & destructio. 190
units.tr: §. D. 4. The eternity of God is demonstrated. 5. Its idea. The definition of Boethius is not exact. 6. Eternity does not coexist with time, nor time with it. 7. The essences of things are not properly eternal. 8. Things made in eternity do not come to be. 9. If the world had no beginning of existence, it would still not be eternal. It is demonstrated that it had a beginning. 10. The origins and destruction of fictions concerning the eternity and presence of God. 190

units.la: XVII. Constantia. §. A. 1.2. Unde Mentis inconstantia, ejusque remedium. 197
units.tr: XVII. Constancy. §. A. 1.2. Whence the inconstancy of the mind, and its remedy. 197

units.la: §. D. 3. Deus est constantissimus in natura sua & placito. 4. Non obstante rerum inconstantia. 5. De promissis, votis, aliisque mediis quibus homines praetendunt sese constantes reddere. 198
units.tr: §. D. 3. God is most constant in his nature and purpose. 4. Notwithstanding the inconstancy of things. 5. Concerning promises, vows, and other means by which men pretend to make themselves constant. 198

units.la: XVIII. Simplicitas. §. A. 1. Mentis divisio & compositio. 2. quo simplicior certo sensu, eo confusior. 3. Nunquam absolute simplex futura. 200
units.tr: XVIII. Simplicity. §. A. 1. Division and composition of the mind. 2. The simpler a thing is in a certain sense, the more confused it is. 3. It will never be absolutely simple. 200

units.la: §. D. 4. Simplicitas Divina, qua? demonstratur. 5. Difficultates tres. 6. Cur nullum aliud Simplicitatis exemplum sit. 7. Qua distinctio inter attributa Dei sit. Ea simplicitati non obstat. 8. Neque diversitas decretorum. 9. Ut illa adumbretur in materialibus & in Mentibus. 202
units.tr: §. D. 4. The divine simplicity, and how it is demonstrated. 5. Three difficulties. 6. Why there is no other example of simplicity. 7. What distinction there is among the attributes of God. This does not hinder simplicity. 8. Nor does the diversity of decrees. 9. How that simplicity is shadowed forth in material things and in minds. 202

units.la: XIX. Libertas. §. A. 1. Mentis Libertas in quibus. 2. 3. Spontaneitatis. Impetuum gradus unde? Cautela. Motus Deo addictus. Ea a Deo ponitur, nec minuitur ob ejus Potentiam. 4. Datur Indifferentia. 5. Nec obstant difficultates.
units.tr: XIX. Liberty. §. A. 1. In what the liberty of the mind consists. 2. 3. Of spontaneity. Whence the degrees of impulse? Caution. Motion is subject to God. It is posited by God, and is not diminished by his power. 4. Indifference is given. 5. Nor do the difficulties stand in the way.

units.la: 6. An Libertatis creata Idea æqualis Divina vel minor ea sit dicenda? 206
units.tr: 6. Is the created idea of liberty to be called equal to the divine, or less than it? 206

units.la: §. D. 7. In Deo esse Libertatem non-indifferentem. 8. Esse & indifferentem, qua positiva & solius Dei prærogativa. 210
units.tr: §. D. 7. That liberty in God is not indifferent. 8. That it is also indifferent, as a positive prerogative of God alone. 210

units.la: XX. Impassibilitas. §. A. 1. Passiones Animæ in genere, multæ. 2. Mirabilis Dei de hisce dispensatio. 3.4. Sensationes non tendunt in falsum. 4. Ex solis sensationibus regere corpus, brutum est. 212
units.tr: XX. Impassibility. §. A. 1. The passions of the soul in general, many. 2. The wonderful dispensation of God concerning these. 3.4. Sensations do not tend toward falsehood. 4. To govern the body by sensations alone is brutish. 212

units.la: §. D. 5. Deus nil in se patitur. Ejus Sensus perfectissimus. 216
units.tr: §. D. 5. God suffers nothing in himself. His sense is most perfect. 216

units.la: XXI. Justitia. §. A. 1. Imperfectiones voluntariae, injusta. 2. Justitia in homine. 3. Injustitia, adductis aliquot exemplis. 4. Ea hominem, non vero Deum attingunt. 217
units.tr: XXI. Justice. §. A. 1. Voluntary imperfections are unjust. 2. Justice in man. 3. Injustice, with several examples adduced. 4. These touch man, but not God. 217

units.la: §.D.5. In Dei natura, placito, opere, injustitia est. 6. Ea ultra vindictam mali extendenda. 7. Justitia vindicativa ut Deo essentialis. ut postulat satisfactionem. 8. Nempe ut peccator sit æternum miser. 9. Vel ex amore Dei summe doleat. 10. Quod interventum subjecti praestantissimi & innocentissimi requisivit. 11. Conscientia hisce suffragatur quoad jus. veritas facti ex revelatione & experientia depromenda. 219
units.tr: §. D. 5. There is injustice in the nature, purpose, and work of God. 6. It must be extended beyond the punishment of evil. 7. Vindictive justice is essential to God, as it demands satisfaction. 8. Namely, that the sinner be eternally miserable. 9. Or that he grieve intensely out of love for God. 10. Which required the intervention of a most excellent and innocent subject. 11. Conscience supports these things as to right; the truth of the fact is to be drawn from revelation and experience. 219

units.la: XXII. Veracitas. §. A. 1. Mendacii, fraudis, perfidia, &c. injustitia. 223
units.tr: XXII. Truthfulness. §. A. 1. Injustice of lying, fraud, treachery, etc. 223

units.la: §.D. 2. Veracitas Dei in promissis. 3. Promissa verbalia & naturalia. 224
units.tr: §. D. 2. The truthfulness of God in his promises. 3. Verbal and natural promises. 224

units.la: XXIII. Sanctitas. §. A. 1. Anima impuritas & Sanctitas. 225
units.tr: XXIII. Holiness. §. A. 1. Impurity and holiness of the soul. 225

units.la: §. D. 2. 3. 4. Dei Sanctitas qua? demonstratur. Declaratur in creaturis viis oppositis. Ad justitiam referenda. 226
units.tr: §. D. 2. 3. 4. How the holiness of God is demonstrated. It is declared in creatures by opposite ways. It is to be referred to justice. 226

units.la: XXIV. Infinitas. §. A. 1. Mens augmenti capax est limitata, non habito respectu ad spatia. 227
units.tr: XXIV. Infinity. §. A. 1. The limited mind is capable of increase, without regard to spaces. 227

units.la: §. D. 2. Deus positive infinitus. 3. Non spatii extensione, sed Cogitationis perfectione. 4. Infinitum sufficienter concipitur. 5. De repraesentatione Infiniti. 6. Qua requirit Deum existentem. ibid.
units.tr: §. D. 2. God is positively infinite. 3. Not by extension in space, but by perfection of thought. 4. The infinite is sufficiently conceived. 5. On the representation of the infinite. 6. What it requires: that God exists. ibid.

units.la: XXV. Immortalitas. §. A. 1. Anima, si Deus
units.tr: XXV. Immortality. §. A. 1. The soul, if God willed, could come to nothing.

units.la: si Deus vellet, ad nihil devenire posset.
units.tr: If God willed, it could come to nothing.

units.la: 2. Ex quibus demonstranda sit Animæ immortalitas. 3. Mortis significationes generaliores. Anima non moritur ut corpus. 4. Ea quadruplici sensu mortalis, imo mortua dici potest. 5. De modis mentis an cessaturi? De substantia Mentis quæstio præcipua, Num Deo placuerit eam tantum durare donec corpus dissolvatur? 6. Id sine revelatione solvi potest.
units.tr: 2. From which things the immortality of the soul is to be demonstrated. 3. More general meanings of death. The soul does not die as the body does. 4. In a fourfold sense it can be called mortal, indeed dead. 5. Whether the modes of the mind are to cease? The principal question concerning the substance of the mind: whether God has willed that it endure only until the body is dissolved? 6. This can be resolved without revelation.

units.la: 7. Corporis Menti uniti dissolutio non infert Mentis annihilationem. 8. Nodus præcipuus de Animæ Immortalitate. Solvitur eadem de causa qua allegatur. 9. Animæ immortalitatis Demonstrationes primariæ ex Dei attributis. 10. Ex Justitia. 11. Ex Constantia. 12. Ex Sapientia. 13. Ex vindicativa Justitia. 14. Ex Sanctitate. 15. 16. Ex veracitate. 17. 18. 19. 20. De statu Animarum post mortem. 231
units.tr: 7. The dissolution of the body united to the mind does not entail the annihilation of the mind. 8. The principal knot concerning the immortality of the soul. It is solved on the same ground on which it is alleged. 9. The primary demonstrations of the immortality of the soul from the attributes of God. 10. From justice. 11. From constancy. 12. From wisdom. 13. From vindictive justice. 14. From holiness. 15, 16. From truthfulness. 17, 18, 19, 20. Concerning the state of souls after death. 231

units.la: §.D.21. Deus est immortalis sensu nobiliori quam sit Anima, sibique soli proprio. 244
units.tr: §. D. 21. God is immortal in a nobler sense than the soul is, and proper to himself alone. 244

units.la: XXVI. Gloria, §. A. 1. Gloriæ Mentis de se occasio nulla est. 2. Probatur id ex vano Mentis de se phantasmate. 3. Ex consideratione operantis Dei. 4. Ex consideratione operis ipsius in genere. 5. Ex consideratione operis quatenus id est Cogitans. 245
units.tr: XXVI. Glory. §. A. 1. The mind has no occasion for glory in itself. 2. This is proved from the vain phantasm of the mind concerning itself. 3. From consideration of God as the one who acts. 4. From consideration of the work itself in general. 5. From consideration of the work as it is thinking. 245

units.la: §.D. 6. Gloria Deo Essentialis. 7. Gloria relativa ejus in creaturis. Gloria quomodo datur Deo. Deus cur glorificandus & laudandus? 247
units.tr: §. D. 6. Glory is essential to God. 7. His relative glory in creatures. How glory is given to God. Why God is to be glorified and praised. 247

units.la: XXVII. §. 1. Reflexio ad præcedentia. 2. Attributorum Divinorum distributio generalior. 3. Specialior. 4. Via facilior ad ea cognoscenda. 5. 6. Hic non harendum, sed ad notitiam infusam tendendum. 7. Remoto obstaculo, nempe Malo, de quo postea tractabitur. 248
units.tr: XXVII. §. 1. Reflection on what precedes. 2. A more general distribution of the divine attributes. 3. A more specific one. 4. An easier way to know them. 5, 6. Here one should not linger, but aim at infused knowledge. 7. The obstacle removed, namely Evil, which will be treated afterwards. 248

units.la: LIBER IV. De Malo sive Peccato.
units.tr: Book IV. On Evil, or Sin.

units.la: CAP. I. §. 1.---6. De iis quæ ad sequentia sunt prænotanda. 253
units.tr: Ch. I. §§ 1–6. On the things that must be noted in advance for what follows. 253

units.la: II. §. 1. Generalissima Notio peccati.
units.tr: Ch. II. § 1. The most general notion of sin.

units.la: 2--6. A peccato generalius subducuntur quæ ad illud non spectant, Deus, Dei placitum, Dei opus ut à Deo est: Absolutum nihil, nihil existentiæ, & nihil admixtum realitati, quatenus hoc à Deo est. 7. Non quatenus ab homine. 255
units.tr: 2–6. Things that do not pertain to sin are set aside more generally: God, the pleasure of God, the work of God insofar as it is from God: the absolutely nothing, the nothing of existence, and the nothing mixed into reality, insofar as this is from God. 7. Not insofar as it is from man. 255

units.la: III. §. 1. 2. 3. 4. Specialius quod à peccato subducendum (1) in corpore. 5. (2) in sensibus & passionibus. 6.7.8. (3) Mentis materiale & formale, error, facultates, habitus, actus, ignorantia, notitia, spontaneitas, ut ad illud se habeant? Non est explicita Dei rejectio. 9. Peccati specialior designatio. 10. Ad illud reflexio non requiritur. 259
units.tr: Ch. III. §§ 1, 2, 3, 4. More specifically, what is to be set aside from sin: (1) in the body. 5. (2) in the senses and passions. 6, 7, 8. (3) of the mind, the material and the formal: error, faculties, habits, acts, ignorance, knowledge, spontaneity, insofar as they stand in relation to it? There is no explicit rejection of God. 9. A more specific designation of sin. 10. Reflection upon it is not required. 259

units.la: IV. §. 1. De Libertate notiones clariores. 2. 3. 4. De indifferentia, eam dari. 5. ea est multiplex. 6--12. In creatura non est positiva, sed negativa. demonstratur; repulsis contrarii probationibus. 13. Ejus termini duo. 14. Peccati specialissima designatio. 265
units.tr: Ch. IV. § 1. Clearer notions of liberty. 2, 3, 4. Concerning indifference, that it is given. 5. It is manifold. 6–12. In the creature it is not positive but negative. This is demonstrated, the proofs to the contrary being refuted. 13. Its two terms. 14. The most specific designation of sin. 265

units.la: V. §. 1. Difficultates notabiles ex præcedentibus septem. 2. 3. An homo debeat ex se aliquid positivi agere? 4 Num status negativus faveat negligentiæ? 5.6.7. An Mens possit in illo manere? quanta perfectiones eum sequuntur? 8. Num inde Menti occasio gloriandi? 8.9.10. Admisso peccato an maneat indifferentia? Quæ causa ad sublationem peccati? Primariæ species peccati tres. 11.12. De præscientia Dei & Regimine circa peccata. 13. An Deus indifferentiam tollere potuerit? & cur non sustulerit? 272
units.tr: Ch. V. § 1. Notable difficulties arising from the seven preceding. 2, 3. Must man of himself do anything positive? 4. Does a negative state favour negligence? 5, 6, 7. Can the mind remain in that state? What perfections follow it? 8. Does the mind thence have an occasion for boasting? 8, 9, 10. Once sin is admitted, does indifference remain? What is the cause of the removal of sin? The primary kinds of sin are three. 11, 12. Concerning the foreknowledge of God and his governance with respect to sins. 13. Could God have removed indifference, and why did he not remove it? 272

units.la: VI. Proprietates peccati, sive denominationes nonnullæ exponuntur. 1. Quod sit Injustum. 2. Negatio Dei. 3. Privatio. 4. Adhærentia sibi ipsi, appropriatio, propria voluntas, &c. 5. Superbia. 6. Peccator ut reputandus. 285
units.tr: Ch. VI. The properties of sin, or certain designations, are set forth. 1. That it is unjust. 2. The denial of God. 3. Privation. 4. Adherence to oneself, appropriation, self-will, etc. 5. Pride. 6. The sinner as he is to be reckoned. 285

units.la: VII. §. 1. 2. 3. 4. Pauca de extensione vel repressione peccati in actionibus & in radice. 5. 6. De discrimine inter peccata proborum & improborum. 7. De certitudine sui status. 8. Conclusio. 289
units.tr: Ch. VII. §§ 1, 2, 3, 4. A few things on the extension or repression of sin in actions and in the root. 5, 6. On the distinction between the sins of the upright and of the wicked. 7. On the certainty of one's own state. 8. Conclusion. 289

units.la: FINIS
units.tr: THE END

units.la: Operarum errata quibus pervertitur sensus sic emendate leges.
units.tr: Errata of the printer, by which the sense is perverted; read them corrected as follows.
